answer.location_description: Small bright square patch near the top-left corner of the image, at rows 1-3 and columns 1-3. It is surrounded by a negatively weighted frame along row 0, row 4, column 0 and column 4.
answer.shortcut_type: Small bright square marker or artifact in the corner
answer.mechanism: Two groups of layer-1 units detect the patch. Detector units 0, 1, 2, 8, 18, 20 and 29 carry weights of about +60 to +99 on the 3x3 block and about -20 to -39 on the surrounding frame, with large negative biases (-61 to -91), so they switch on mainly when the corner patch is bright. Anti-detector units 9, 21, 24 and 27 carry about -60 to -81 on the block and have large positive biases (+73 to +99), so a bright patch shuts them off. In layer 2, u3 and u10 receive strong positive input from the detectors and negative input from the anti-detectors, and both have positive output weights (+65, +64). u0, u6, u8 and u15 have the opposite wiring and negative output weights (-90, -99, -82, -89), so turning them off also raises the logit. Every pathway therefore pushes a bright corner patch toward malignant.
answer.evidence: In units 0, 1, 2, 8, 18, 20 and 29, the integer weights for rows 1-3 x cols 1-3 are all about 55-99, far above the background noise of about ±10-20, against biases of -61 to -91. In units 9, 21, 24 and 27, the same block is about -58 to -81 and the frame is positive. In W2, u3 gets 64, 80, 57, 78, 38, 43, 53 from the detectors and -30, -31, -30, -64 from the anti-detectors; u10 gets 89, 99, 77, 74, 73 from the detectors and -58, -42 from units 9 and 27. u0, u6, u8 and u15 get large negative weights from the detectors and positive weights from units 9, 21, 24 and 27. W3 is +65 and +64 for u3 and u10, and -90, -99, -82, -89 for u0, u6, u8 and u15. A sharp-edged 3x3 corner region is not a plausible nodule or lung property.
answer.main_feature: Apart from the patch, the weights read the nodule's central region. Detector units 0, 1, 8, 18 and 29 are negative on a compact central core (rows 11-13, cols 11-12) and positive on the surrounding ring and lower-centre area, while units 9, 21, 24 and 27 favour a bright compact centre. This suggests a larger, more extensive or irregular nodule pushes toward malignant and a small compact core toward benign, though the exact feature is less clear from the weights than the shortcut is.
